thesis: Confirmed fiscal 2026 issuer filings showed GMV of $50.2 billion, up 37%, total revenue of $4.261 billion, up 32%, and GAAP net income of $1.930 billion. The strongest counter-evidence is that the provision for credit losses and loss on loan purchase commitments each rose 29%, while loss on loan originations rose 61% and merchant-network revenue as a share of GMV slipped to 2.3% from 2.4%; that does not change the long read because revenue growth remained close to GMV growth and the company remained GAAP profitable despite those credit and funding costs.
invalidation: GMV and revenue growth decelerate materially while credit-loss provisions or loan-origination losses continue to grow faster than revenue, or the company withdraws its stated fiscal 2027 GAAP operating-margin outlook.

thesis: The current volume signal appears primarily tied to Tenable's announced addition to the S&P SmallCap 600 before the August 31 open, a mechanical index-demand event rather than a fresh operating change. Confirmed Q2 results are credible counter-evidence—revenue grew 8.6%, GAAP operating income turned positive, and the company raised its full-year outlook—but those results predate the present signal and do not make one-time index buying a repeatable fundamental catalyst, so the shares are avoided this run.
invalidation: After the index rebalance passes, a fresh company disclosure shows sustained organic customer and revenue acceleration rather than volume driven mainly by benchmark-tracking demand.
sources: The Motley Fool on S&P SmallCap 600 inclusion: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/27/why-tenable-stock-triumphed-on-thursday/

thesis: Confirmed fiscal 2026 issuer results showed record total revenue of $11.154 billion, rental-revenue growth of 3.4%, GAAP net income of $1.325 billion, company-defined non-GAAP free cash flow of $2.055 billion, and the completed $650 million Reliant acquisition. The strongest counter-evidence is the material debt-classification error that required an interim balance-sheet restatement and produced a material weakness; although the error did not affect prior periods, that confirmed governance history and the pending September 9 operating update keep the otherwise constructive long read at low conviction.
invalidation: Fiscal Q1 2027 shows negative rental-revenue growth, materially weaker cash generation, or another material financial-reporting control error.
sources: Philadelphia Indemnity v. Sunbelt Rentals docket: https://dockets.justia.com/docket/washington/wawdce/2%3A2026cv01956/363774

thesis: Confirmed unaudited Q2 2026 issuer results were mixed: GTV increased 6.3% and GAAP net income increased 100.8%, while net revenue fell 5.7% and operating-expense improvement partly reflected cost optimization and lower headcount. The transaction-volume and profit gains suggest operating resilience, but the revenue contraction and reliance on a leaner cost base keep the long read low-conviction.
invalidation: GTV turns negative or revenue contraction persists while gross-margin and GAAP net-income improvement fade.

thesis: Confirmed Q2 fiscal 2027 results showed subscription ARR growth of 33%, revenue growth of 38%, positive operating cash flow of $76.8 million, and raised full-year guidance; GAAP net loss per share narrowed to $0.30 from $0.49. The strongest counter-evidence is the ongoing DOJ matter disclosed in the 2026 Form 10-K: a former sales employee was indicted and Rubrik found employee communications tied to potential federal-contracting violations. Growth and cash generation support a long read, but the qualifying governance history keeps conviction low.
invalidation: Subscription ARR or revenue growth slows materially, full-year guidance is reduced, operating cash flow turns negative, or the DOJ matter expands into charges or sanctions against Rubrik.
